Check a scar table before analysis

Source: R/check_scars.R
check_scars.Rd

Reports in one message what the scar-pattern functions would make of a scar table: how many cores and scars it holds, which scars would be left out (missing coordinates, zero length, shorter than min_length), which cores have fewer than three usable scars, and whether the keep columns are constant within each core. Run it once after reading the data.

Usage

check_scars(
  data,
  id_col = "ID",
  start_cols = c("Start_X", "Start_Y", "Start_Z"),
  end_cols = c("End_X", "End_Y", "End_Z"),
  min_length = 0,
  keep = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per scar and the columns named by id_col, start_cols and end_cols. Scars of all cores are stacked.

id_col

Name of the core ID column. Default "ID".

start_cols, end_cols

Names of the start- and end-point coordinate columns (X, Y, Z). Defaults Start_X/Y/Z and End_X/Y/Z, the columns the scars are recorded in. The aligned columns of align_scar_batch() (s_x... and e_x...) give the same results: these indices do not change when a core is rotated or moved.

min_length

Scars shorter than this (in the units of the coordinates) are left out. Default 0 (keep all). Use it to repeat an analysis without small scars, for example min_length = 10 for 10 mm.

keep

Names of per-core columns (for example "Typology") to carry into the output. Each must be constant within a core.

Value

Invisibly, a tibble with one row per core: the ID column, the keep columns, n_rows (rows in the table), n_missing, n_zero, n_short (rows left out for each reason), n_scar (usable scars) and enough (n_scar of at least 3).

See also

spi_ei_batch(), cpi_pra_batch(), spharm_spatiodirection()

Examples

d <- data.frame(ID = rep(c("a", "b"), c(4, 2)),
                Start_X = c(0, 1, 2, 3, 0, 1), Start_Y = 0, Start_Z = 0,
                End_X = c(1, 1, 3, 5, 1, 2), End_Y = c(1, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1),
                End_Z = 0)
check_scars(d)
#> 2 core(s), 6 scar row(s); usable scars per core: 2-3 (median 2.5).
#> Left out 1 scar(s) of zero length (a).
#> 1 core(s) have fewer than 3 usable scars and will be NA: b.
